results.content: The Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge cooled more than expected but remained elevated well above target in August as consumers continued to face price pressures. The Commerce Department on Wednesday reported that the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) index rose 0.3% on a monthly basis in August and was up 3.4% from a year ago. Core PCE, which excludes volatile measurements of food and energy prices, was up 0.2% on a monthly basis and 3% year over year. Those readings follow the BEA's annual benchmark revisions to PCE inflation data, which lowered July's readings for headline PCE from 3.7% to 3.4% and core PCE from 3.3% to 3%.
